zh.question: 为什么有的火山变成绿山，有的仍光秃秃，还有的山顶塌成了湖盆？
zh.observe: 先选大室山式火山锥，进入“植物怎样回来”，观察冷却、岩缝积土和种子到达。在相同进度切换湿润、干旱、寒冷与厚灰覆盖，看看小苗在哪里长起来。再选火山湖，依次看岩浆撤出、支撑减弱、岩体下沉，最后才让水进入。陆地案例还可以进入“为什么会喷发”，改变岩层阻碍，比较岩浆能否到达地表。

academic.title: 从地下活动到喷发：贯通、气体与流变
academic.body: 岩浆来自深部岩石的部分熔融。储存系统可包含不同深度的熔体、晶体和相连岩床；补给可改变过压，但浮力、围岩应力、构造张裂、脱气和冷却也影响岩脉传播。这里只演示一次补给驱动的情境：贯通后排出降低过压，未贯通则保留地下侵入体。条形指标没有真实单位，不能由此推算喷发时间或概率。 岩浆上升时围压下降，溶解的挥发组分可以出溶形成气泡，气泡也会膨胀。流变和气体逸出影响熔岩溢流、喷泉或碎裂；温度、成分、晶体、供浆与外来水同样重要，低黏度并不保证没有爆炸。VEI 主要依据爆炸性喷出物体积，并结合喷发柱等证据，不等于全部能量或危险程度，也不是熔岩流量的刻度。本页补给与岩层阻碍共同决定示意岩脉是否贯通地表；只有贯通后才开始喷出物的独立演化。

academic.title: 不同地貌，来自不同的物质与历史
academic.body: 较易流动的熔岩可多次铺展，形成宽缓的盾状火山；熔岩与碎屑共同累积，可构成成层火山。火山渣锥由喷口周围堆积的火山渣等碎屑建立，大室山还伴随山麓熔岩流。山形在喷发时已形成，并不是熄灭后才变出的形态；后续侵蚀、风化和植被覆盖继续修改它。大室山的草坡景观还与传统山烧管理有关。海底火山同样靠累积物质生长，但压力、冷却与岩浆和水相互作用会影响喷发产物。只有累积足够的部分海底火山会长成岛。 裸岩变绿还需要生态恢复：风化产物、外来尘土及有机物积累，种子或孢子到达，并有适宜水分、温度和基质。干旱、寒冷、土层薄、排水快，以及新的熔岩或厚灰覆盖等，都可延缓或中断恢复。植物并无统一到场顺序，也不必经过相同年数或最终成为森林。

academic.title: 湖泊、安静与活动潜力是不同的问题
academic.body: 塌陷案例中，岩浆沿通道撤出会改变储存区压力和对上覆岩体的支撑；上方岩体自重仍在，失稳后可沿断裂下沉。裂隙和沉降发生在后来积水之前，地下不必先出现永久空洞，也并非每次喷发都会触发塌陷。 火山口和塌陷破火山口可以提供蓄水凹地；是否形成湖泊取决于水量平衡和渗透性等条件。火山湖装的是后来补给的水，熔岩湖装的是熔融岩石。有湖不代表火山已永久熄灭，Crater Lake 所在火山中心仍有未来喷发潜力。休眠常指喷发之间的间歇；被认为熄灭则需要结合地质年代、构造和供浆背景，判断也可能修订。草坡、湖水、没有烟或某个固定年数都不能代替这些证据，旧喷口不再活动也不排除火山区别处产生新喷口。

zh.misconception: 这些案例没有共同的“喷发、死亡、成湖”倒计时。长草和积水不能证明火山已熄灭，海底火山也不一定最终成岛。
zh.boundary: 这些是选择了特定条件的概念案例，不是实测重建或危险预测。地貌故事和一次喷发各有进度；示意堆积、侵蚀、植被和水量平衡没有统一真实时标。

narration.label: 选择一座火山
narration.text: 火山有很多模样。宽宽的山、圆圆的小山、藏在海里的大山，甚至山上的湖，都可能留下火山活动的故事。先选一座，把剖面打开。我们要跟着岩浆，看看它能不能到地面，再看留下了什么。
narration.cue: 逐一展示五张案例卡，进入大室山式火山渣锥并打开剖面。

narration.label: 喷出的东西留下来了
narration.text: 先往地下看：新的岩浆补进来，周围岩石受到挤压。岩浆沿裂缝往上走，里面的气泡也会变大。走到地面，才会喷出熔岩和碎屑；有时候，它会停在地下。试着增大岩层阻碍，再看一次。喷出来的东西落下、冷却，一点一点留下山。盾状火山铺得宽，成层火山留下熔岩和碎屑，大室山式的小山则堆起许多火山渣。
narration.cue: 从堆积初期推进到冷却；比较三种山形，再进入一次喷发并暂停。

narration.label: 海水和湖水加入故事
narration.text: 再看看山里的湖。先不要放水！跟着橙色岩浆走：它去了别处，上面沉甸甸的岩石还在。支撑减弱，裂缝扩大，岩体沿着断裂往下沉，才留下低洼的盆地。雨水、融雪后来汇进来，才可能变成湖。水如果都漏走了，有个大坑也留不住湖。海里的火山则还有另一条故事：岩石在水下一次次堆起来，有些才长成岛。
narration.cue: 火山湖依次停在13%、23%、36%、72%，追踪岩浆、裂隙、相同岩层和后来的水。

narration.label: 安静之后还有故事
narration.text: 喷发停了，山没有消失。岩石慢慢凉下来，缝里留住细土和水，风和动物把种子带来。有种子就一定会绿吗？换成很干或很冷的环境，再看看小苗。新的厚灰还可能把它们盖住。大室山今天像一顶草帽，还受到人们长期山烧管理。长草、没有草，都不能单独告诉我们火山以后会不会喷。
narration.cue: 进入“植物怎样回来”，观看冷却、岩缝积土、种子到达，再在末阶段比较四种环境；厚灰情境回看65%到80%的植被减少。

en.question: Why do some volcanoes turn green, some stay bare, and some summits collapse into lake basins?
en.observe: Choose the Omuroyama-style cone and open How plants return. Follow cooling, soil collecting in cracks and arriving seeds. At the same progress, compare wet, dry, cold and thick-ash conditions to see where seedlings establish. Then choose the volcanic lake: follow magma withdrawal, reduced support and sinking rock before water arrives. On land, also open Why does it erupt and change rock barriers to compare whether magma reaches the surface.

academic.title: From unrest to eruption: connection, gas and flow
academic.body: Magma originates through partial melting at depth. Storage may contain melt, crystals and connected sills at several levels. Recharge can change overpressure, while buoyancy, host-rock stress, tectonic extension, degassing and cooling also affect dike propagation. This is one recharge-driven episode: discharge reduces overpressure after connection, while a stalled intrusion remains underground. The bars have no physical units and cannot predict eruption timing or probability. As magma rises, falling pressure allows dissolved volatiles to exsolve and gas bubbles to expand. Flow properties and gas escape influence effusion, fountains and fragmentation. Temperature, composition, crystals, magma supply and external water also matter; low viscosity does not rule out explosions. VEI primarily uses explosive ejecta volume together with plume evidence. It is not a score for total energy or hazard, nor a measure of lava discharge. Supply and rock barriers jointly determine whether the illustrative dike reaches the surface. Only then does the separate evolution of surface products begin.

academic.title: Different landscapes record different materials and histories
academic.body: Repeated fluid lava flows can build a broad shield; lava and fragment deposits can form a composite volcano. Scoria cones grow from fragments deposited around a vent. Omuroyama also produced lava from its foot. Its cone formed during eruption, not as a consequence of extinction. Later weathering, erosion and vegetation modify the surface; traditional burning also maintains Omuroyama’s grassland. Submarine volcanoes likewise accumulate material, while pressure, cooling and magma–water interaction influence products. Only some accumulate enough material to become islands. Ecological recovery additionally needs suitable substrate, water and temperatures, along with arriving seeds or spores. Weathered grains, windblown dust and organic material accumulate. Drought, cold, thin soils, rapid drainage, new lava or thick ash can delay or interrupt recovery. There is no universal sequence of organisms, fixed timescale or inevitable forest endpoint.

academic.title: Lakes, quiet intervals and future activity are different questions
academic.body: In the collapse example, magma withdrawal changes reservoir pressure and support for overlying rock. Its weight remains, and unstable rock can subside along faults. Fracturing and subsidence precede later lake filling; a permanent empty cavern is unnecessary, and not every eruption causes collapse. Craters and collapse calderas can provide water-retaining depressions. Lake formation depends on the water balance, permeability and other conditions. A volcanic lake contains water supplied later; a lava lake contains molten rock. A lake does not establish extinction: the volcanic center at Crater Lake retains future eruption potential. Dormancy commonly describes an interval between eruptions. An extinction assessment needs geological ages, tectonic setting and magma-supply history, and may be revised. Grass, water, absent emissions or a fixed number of quiet years cannot replace that evidence. An inactive old vent does not exclude new vents elsewhere in its field.

en.misconception: There is no shared eruption–extinction–lake countdown. Grass and water do not establish extinction, and submarine volcanoes do not inevitably become islands.
en.boundary: These cases select particular conditions; they are neither surveyed reconstructions nor hazard forecasts. Landscape history and one eruption have independent timelines. Deposition, erosion, vegetation and water balance do not share a calibrated real timescale.

narration.label: Choose a volcano
narration.text: Volcanoes have many shapes. A broad mountain, a round cone, a mountain under the sea and even a lake can tell a volcanic story. Choose one and open its cutaway. Follow magma to see whether it reaches the surface, then what remains.
narration.cue: Show the five case cards, enter the Omuroyama-style cone and open the cutaway.

narration.label: Erupted material stays
narration.text: Look underground first. New magma enters and pushes on the surrounding rock. It moves upward along cracks, and its gas bubbles can grow. Lava and fragments appear only after it reaches the surface; sometimes magma stops below. Increase the rock barriers and try again. Erupted material lands and cools, gradually leaving a mountain. Shields spread broadly, composite volcanoes collect lava and fragments, and an Omuroyama-style cone piles up scoria.
narration.cue: Advance deposition through cooling, compare the three shapes, then pause within the eruption detail.

narration.label: Sea and lake water join the story
narration.text: Now look at a lake in a mountain. Do not add water yet! Follow the orange magma as it moves away. The heavy rock above remains. As support weakens, fractures grow and rock sinks along faults, leaving a basin. Rain and melting snow can collect later. If water leaks away, even a large basin may stay dry. Underwater volcanoes have another story: repeated deposits build up, and only some become islands.
narration.cue: Pause the lake case at 13%, 23%, 36% and 72%, tracing magma, fractures, the same rock layer and later water.

narration.label: When the mountain is quiet
narration.text: The eruption stops, but the mountain remains. Rock cools, cracks collect fine material and water, and wind or animals bring seeds. Are seeds enough to turn it green? Try a dry or cold environment and watch the seedlings. Fresh thick ash may bury them too. Omuroyama looks like a grassy hat today partly because people maintain its grassland through traditional burning. Grass, or its absence, cannot by itself tell us whether a volcano will erupt again.
narration.cue: Open How plants return, observe cooling, soil in cracks and seed arrival, then compare four environments at the endpoint. Replay 65–80% under thick ash to see vegetation decline.
